$comment: What tools/status.mjs (npm run status) can't read from the repository. Everything else in docs/status.md comes from the lesson files, lessons.ts, review-queue.json and pending-photos.json.

Per course: student (default for its lessons: done | pending), gemini ('never' = no copy edit yet and not queued; leave out when the review queue says it all), geminiNote, facts (pending | 'done YYYY-MM-DD ...'), expectsPhotos (true: a written lesson with no photo counts as awaiting photos), note (one line under the course heading), planned (lessons in an outline that are not yet in lessons.ts: { id, n, code, title, teaches, branch }). A course with no folder yet (only an outline) is listed by its key with a title, an order and its planned lessons, each with a code and a branch title.

Per lesson, under lessons.<id>: student, facts, gemini ('done' to clear a course-wide 'never'), images (what picture is missing or a stand-in), noPhotos (true: needs none), about (a plainer summary than its teaches line), note.
When a thread finishes a step for a lesson, change it here (or in the queue it came from) and run npm run status.

clouds.note: The oldest course. Its prose went through several student read-throughs (Oct 2026) and a physics review of the sky lab (3 Nov), but never a Gemini copy edit or a full fact check.

fog.about: What a cloud is made of, how a calm clear night makes fog and stratus, and how rising air builds fair-weather cumulus.

low-sky.about: Stable and unstable air, the lid that flattens heaps into stratocumulus, and why a deep cloud rains when a dark thin one doesn't; nimbostratus.

middle-sky.about: The three height floors, how the Latin names fit together, and three field checks for a cloud's height; altocumulus, cirrocumulus and cirrus.

ice-realm.about: Mares' tails, contrails, the 22° halo and altostratus's frosted sun, read as a warm front's countdown 12 to 24 hours ahead.

giants.about: Latent heat and conditional instability, the morning signs of an afternoon storm, anvils, gust fronts and the 30-30 lightning rule.

front.about: Lows and their fronts, the barometer, why warm fronts soak and cold fronts squall, the crossed-winds rule, and reading rain on radar.

local-sky.about: Rain shadows, standing mountain waves and lens clouds, supercooled water, rime and freezing rain, and how ice crystals make rain.

seeding.about: The 1946 dry ice and silver iodide experiments, which clouds seeding can and can't help, and how randomised trials tested it.

wind.about: How pressure pushes the wind, how the turning Earth bends it along the isobars, friction near the ground, and the jet stream.

coast.about: Why the coast from Seattle to San Francisco hardly ever thunders: a cold sea, a lid of sinking air and the marine layer.

rivers.about: Why the Northwest's rain comes from October to April: the storm track, atmospheric rivers, snow level and the Puget Sound convergence zone.

violent.about: Why a few thunderstorms last all evening and drop big hail: the energy a rising bubble gains, the cap that stores it, and wind shear.

tornado.about: Where a tornado's spin comes from (a horizontal roll tipped up and stretched by an updraft), wall clouds, hook echoes and the EF scale.

hurricane.about: How tropical showers become a hurricane: the trade winds, a heat engine run on warm sea, the eye, what kills one, and storm surge.

winter-fog.about: Why a basin can stay foggy for weeks in winter while the hills are sunny: the cold pool, other kinds of fog, rime and freezing rain.

east-wind.about: Dust walls raised by storms whose rain never lands, and why wind coming down off the Cascades arrives hot and dry; the Gorge and the Santa Ana.

fungi.title: Fungi (working title)
fungi.note: Outline only, not yet approved: https://claude.ai/artifact/3um9m4dasG3fu9D8U2Vthh (4 Nov 2026). How fungi work and their kinds, lichens included; not about edible fungi or foraging. 16 trunk lessons and branches L, N, M.

planned.title: The ring in the meadow
planned.teaches: A mushroom is only the fruit of a hidden net of threads; a fairy ring is one fungus spreading outward for centuries

planned.title: Closer to us than to plants
planned.teaches: Why fungi are a kingdom of their own: chitin walls, digestion outside the body, and DNA that puts them beside animals

planned.title: Eating from the outside
planned.teaches: How a hypha grows at its tip, digests food outside itself, and how a mycelium searches and moves food

planned.title: Seven trillion spores
planned.teaches: How fungi spread by spores, how gills launch them, and why most land close while a few cross oceans

planned.title: Twenty thousand sexes
planned.teaches: Mating types, fused threads and the two-nucleus stage of a mushroom's life

planned.title: Sacs and clubs
planned.teaches: The main groups of fungi told apart by how they make spores

planned.title: The yeast that wastes its sugar
planned.teaches: Single-celled fungi, fermentation, and why yeast makes alcohol even with oxygen

planned.title: The gap in the coal
planned.teaches: White and brown rot, lignin, and whether wood-rotting fungi ended the age of coal

planned.title: Do trees share through fungi?
planned.teaches: The two kinds of root fungi and what the evidence shows about carbon passing between trees

planned.title: A lichen is two (or three)
planned.teaches: A fungus farming algae, and how drying out and waking lets lichens live on bare rock

planned.title: The mould on Fleming's plate
planned.teaches: Fungal chemical weapons, penicillin, and resistance

planned.title: Four billion chestnuts
planned.teaches: How fungal plant diseases spread, imported blights, two-host rusts, and the water mould of the Irish famine

planned.title: The frogs that went quiet
planned.teaches: The chytrid killing frogs, white-nose syndrome in bats, and the fungus that steers ants

planned.title: The largest living thing?
planned.teaches: Telling one fungus from another with mating tests and DNA; Michigan's humongous Armillaria

planned.title: A trunk with no leaves
planned.teaches: How a Devonian fossil eight metres tall is weighed as fungus or not, and fungi with the first land plants

planned.title: A log's hundred years
planned.teaches: Which fungi arrive in a fallen log and in what order, and what they leave behind

planned.title: The lichens that left the city
planned.teaches: Lichens as a gauge of sulphur in the air, and their return since coal smoke ended

planned.title: Dating a moraine by its lichens
planned.teaches: Using the slow steady growth of crust lichens to date bare rock

planned.title: Gardens in the canopy
planned.teaches: Nitrogen-fixing lichens high in old Douglas-firs and what they add to the forest

planned.title: The fungus under the Blue Mountains
planned.teaches: The giant Armillaria of the Malheur forest and root disease in dry Northwest forests

planned.title: Gophers on the pumice
planned.teaches: How pocket gophers brought root fungi back to Mount St Helens' pumice plain

planned.title: The squirrel, the truffle and the owl
planned.teaches: Underground truffles, the flying squirrels that spread them and the owls that eat the squirrels

planned.title: A spore print and a microscope
planned.teaches: How mycologists examine a fungus: spore prints, gills and spores under the microscope

planned.title: Names written in DNA
planned.teaches: Naming fungi by a DNA barcode and finding unseen groups in soil

planned.title: How many kinds of fungi?
planned.teaches: About 150,000 named and 2 to 4 million estimated, and how that estimate is made
